MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, HIGHWAYS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS

Project: Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE)

Project ID: P511605

Credit No.: 7985-LK

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Detailed Design and Construction Supervision for Gurunagar Fisheries Village Cluster – Jaffna and Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour Cluster – Trincomalee

Reference No.: MTHUD/F/9/IRDP/Consultancy/3, MoTHUD

STEP Procurement Activity No.: LK-UDA-PMU-551524-CS-QCBS, World Bank

1.    The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the review and validation of conceptual master plans and feasibility studies; site surveys and engineering investigations; preparation of implementable, climate-resilient detailed designs, Good for Construction drawings, design calculations, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and World Bank-compliant bidding documents; intermittent technical support during works procurement; full-time construction supervision and contract administration; and support during the Defects Liability Period for investments at the Gurunagar Fisheries Village Cluster in Jaffna and the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour Cluster in Trincomalee.

3. The total duration of the assignment is expected to be approximately fifty-four (54) months: Phase A – Detailed Design, Bidding Documents and intermittent procurement support, twelve (12) months, including six (6) months for detailed design and up to six (6) months for procurement support; Phase B – Construction Supervision and Contract Administration, thirty (30) months; and Phase C – Defects Liability Period Support, twelve (12) months.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Media > Procurement > TORs).

5. The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

a. Legal status, core business and institutional experience: The Consultant shall be a legally registered consulting firm with at least ten (10) years of institutional experience in detailed engineering design and construction supervision or contract administration of fisheries harbours, ports, coastal or marine infrastructure, or integrated infrastructure assignments of comparable technical complexity.

b. Comparable assignment experience: Successful completion, during the last ten (10) years, of at least two (2) comparable consultancy assignments. At least one assignment shall have covered both detailed engineering design and construction supervision with contract administration, and at least one assignment shall have included a fisheries harbour, port, coastal or marine infrastructure component. The same assignment may satisfy both requirements.

c. Scale of consultancy experience: Successful completion of at least one (1) comparable consultancy contract with a consultancy services value of not less than USD 1 million or its equivalent. The value shall refer to consulting services and shall exclude the value of construction works. This assignment may also be counted under criterion (b).

d. Coastal and marine technical capability: Demonstrated institutional capability in conducting investigations and studies relating to coastal processes, harbour and coastal engineering and the detailed design of coastal or marine structures.

e. Multidisciplinary and multi-site delivery capability: Demonstrated organisational, technical and managerial capability to mobilise and coordinate a multidisciplinary design team and separate site-based construction supervision teams for two geographically separated project locations.

f. Relevant geographic experience: Experience in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or other coastal and island environments with similar physical, climatic, institutional and implementation conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025).

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours, except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form, in person, by mail or by e-mail, to the address below on or before 14.00hrs on September 08, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20 – Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist)

 

UKRAINE

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project 

Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA

 

Assignment Title: Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

 

Reference No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MOES) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter referred to as Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The Project aims to increase efficiency and improve conditions to ensure quality and transparency in the higher education system of Ukraine.

The purpose of the Consultant's activities is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

for Consulting Services

(Individual Consultant)

Higher Education Coordination Administrative Support Specialist

Procurement No. MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20

Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project

World Bank Loan No. 9238-UA


 

I. BACKGROUND

Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (hereinafter referred to as "IBRD" or the "World Bank") signed Loan Agreement No. 9238-UA in the amount of US$200 million to implement the Ukraine Improving Higher Education for Results Project (hereinafter, the "Project"). The Project is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with support from the World Bank Group.

Project implementation period: 2021-2027.

The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve the efficiency, conditions for quality, and transparency in Ukraine's higher education system.

The Project comprises six components:

  • Component 1: Sector-Wide Improvements to Governance, Financing, Quality and Transparency.
  • Component 2: Alliances and Partnerships for Improved Efficiency and Quality.
  • Component 3: Capacity Building and Education Environment Enhancement.
  • Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring and Evaluation.
  • Component 5: Support to Academic and Social Scholarships for Higher Education Students.
  • Component 6: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC).

The Project will finance two expenditure categories: Category (i) - investments in goods, works, and services, with disbursements made against eligible expenditures; and Category (ii) - transfers to the budget upon fulfilment of certain results-based conditions, with disbursements likewise made against eligible expenditures subject to the achievement of specified results, as set forth in the Loan Agreement and the Project Operations Manual.

Within Part 3 of the Project, specialized consultants are planned to be engaged to support the effective management of the higher education and research system, as well as higher education institutions, and to provide support for the implementation of digital, financial, human resources, and other components of higher education reform at the institutional level.

More detailed information about the Project is available at: https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P171050

These Terms of Reference set out the objective and scope of the consulting services, as well as the qualification requirements for the Consultant.

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to provide administrative and organizational support for the activities of the support team of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in the higher education sector and to coordinate with management, structural units, higher education institutions, the UIHERP Project, and other higher education stakeholders in order to facilitate an effective management process.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

The Consultant's scope of services shall include, but not be limited to:

  • ensure effective working interaction among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, consultants of UIHERP and other stakeholder;
  • collect and consolidate information required for UIHERP implementation;
  • organize the day-to-day work of specialists and consultants of the MoES UIHERP support team;
  • coordinate work-related matters, deadlines, and task priorities;
  • maintain working calendars and records of tasks, deadlines, status, and agreements; send reminders to responsible persons and provide timely notice of delays or the need for management decisions;
  • coordinate the preparation and conduct of working sessions, meetings, events, and visits under the Project; record agreements and monitor follow-up actions;
  • ensure the timely exchange of information among MoES management, structural units, the support consultant team, higher education institutions, partners, and UIHERP;
  • collect, verify for completeness, systematize, and technically format working materials, background information, draft letters, and meeting materials;
  • organize the clearance of documents and materials, track their routing and status, and monitor the completion of assigned tasks;
  • organize the collection of reports from engaged Support Team specialists for the preparation of monthly and other reports required under the Project, and perform other Project implementation tasks within the Consultant's competence;
  • perform other Project-related tasks within the Consultant's competence, as assigned by the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system.

The following outputs and results are expected from the services (the list is not exhaustive):

  • the day-to-day work of MoES specialists, consultants of the higher education support team, and UIHERP is organized;
  • working calendars, task lists, deadlines, status, and agreements are kept up to date; decisions and follow-up actions are recorded and tracked;
  • working meetings, sessions, events, and visits are organized in a timely manner; the necessary materials are prepared and information exchange among the parties involved is ensured;
  • working materials and evidence of task completion are systematized;
  • effective working interaction is ensured among the Deputy Minister, MoES structural units, the support team and UIHERP, higher education institutions, and other higher education stakeholders;
  • the day-to-day work of the team's specialists and consultants is organized.

IV. REPORTING

The Consultant shall report to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator, be accountable to the Deputy Minister of Education and Science of Ukraine responsible for the higher education system, and work under their supervision.

The Consultant shall coordinate their activities with the Project Manager - Head of the Consultant Team and ensure the administrative coordination of specialists and consultants engaged in implementing UIHERP tasks in higher education.

The Consultant shall submit monthly reports in hard copy to the Project Coordinator/Co-Coordinator.

Each monthly report shall include a concise description of the administrative and coordination tasks performed, meetings and events organized, assignments and work processes supported, the status of interaction with engaged specialists, and the materials collected and systematized for UIHERP implementation and reporting. Where necessary, the report shall include agendas, minutes, links, task lists, or other evidence of performance.

V. RESOURCES PROVIDED

MoES shall provide the Consultant in a timely manner with the information necessary to perform the assignment.

MoES may provide the Consultant with a workspace, including the equipment necessary to perform the functions (e.g., a personal computer, communications equipment, and office equipment).

VI. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum requirements (mandatory):

  • a Master's degree or higher;
  • at least three years of professional experience in administrative coordination, project administration, or organizational support for managers or teams in the education sector;
  • experience organizing the work of a team or group of consultants while concurrently managing multiple tasks, deadlines, and clearances;
  • experience preparing working meetings and events, taking minutes or recording agreements, and monitoring their implementation;
  • experience organizing document workflows, clearance processes, and working interaction among structural units, partners, or contractors;
  • skills in collecting, systematizing, and consolidating information for working and reporting materials;
  • strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to work with confidential information, manage multiple tasks, and meet tight deadlines;
  • fluency in Ukrainian;
  • English proficiency at CEFR level B2 or higher;
  • proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, videoconferencing platforms, and digital tools for task management and teamwork.

The following preferred (non-mandatory) qualifications, competencies, and experience will be considered an advantage:

  • an academic background in management, public administration, project management, international relations, political science, or a related field;
  • experience in higher education;
  • experience in the public sector;
  • experience providing administrative support to projects financed by international financial institutions or international technical assistance programs;
  • knowledge of other foreign languages will be considered an advantage.

MoES may invite the most qualified candidates for an interview to clarify information provided in their CVs.

VII. PERIOD AND PLACE OF WORK

The Consultant shall provide the services until 30 June 2027. with the possibility of extending the contract if UIHERP is extended.

The Consultant shall provide the services under this Contract on an ongoing basis throughout its term, with a level of effort equivalent to full-time engagement, to the extent necessary for the proper performance of the tasks specified in these Terms of Reference.

The Client and the Consultant may at any time agree on a different workload based on the actual volume of tasks.

Specific contractual terms and working arrangements shall be discussed and agreed separately.

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org, marina.chubenko@mon.gov.ua indicating the email subject: «MOES-C3-05-SUP-IC-20: [NAME]».

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time September 8, 2026.

If the candidate fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the candidate’s application.

REPUBLIQUE DE GUINEE                                                                                                              

Ministère DES MINES ET DE LA GEOLOGIE (MMG)

MINISTERE DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT et du developpement durable (MEDD) PROJET DE GESTION DES RESSOURCES NATURELLES, MINIERES ET DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT (PGRNME)

 CREDIT IDA N° 6885 – GN ET DON IDA N° 8190 -GN

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

LE RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT CHARGE DE FORMER LES AGENTS DE L’AGENCE GUINEENNE D’EVALUATIONS ENVIRONNEMENTALES (AGEE) SUR L’INTEGRATION DES ENJEUX LIES AU CHANGEMENT CLIMATIQUE, EN PARTICULIER LA SEQUESTRATION ET LA GESTION DES CREDITS CARBONES, AINSI QUE LA COMPENSATION AU TITRE DE LA BIOBIODIVERSITE (CALCUL METRIQUE)

AMI N°11/PGRNME/MEDD/CI/2026

            Date de fin : 08 Septembre 2026

1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

L'Agence Guinéenne d'Évaluations Environnementales (AGEE), établissement public administratif placé sous la tutelle du Ministère de l'Environnement et du Développement Durable, est chargée de la mise en œuvre de la politique nationale en matière d'évaluation environnementale et sociale. À ce titre, elle assure notamment l'examen des Études d'Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES), des Notices d'Impact Environnemental et Social (NIES), des Évaluations Environnementales Stratégiques (EES), le suivi de la mise en œuvre des Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES), les audits environnementaux et sociaux, ainsi que le contrôle de la conformité environnementale des projets et programmes de développement.

Dans un contexte marqué par les changements climatiques, l'érosion accélérée de la biodiversité et l'accroissement des exigences des partenaires techniques et financiers, les évaluations environnementales doivent désormais intégrer de manière systématique les enjeux liés à l'atténuation et à l'adaptation au changement climatique, à la séquestration du carbone, aux marchés des crédits carbone, ainsi qu'aux mécanismes de compensation écologique visant l'atteinte de l'objectif de « zéro perte nette », voire de « gain net de biodiversité ».

Par ailleurs, les exigences des Normes environnementales et sociales de la Banque mondiale, des Normes de performance de la Société financière internationale (IFC), des Standards de la Banque africaine de développement (BAD), ainsi que des cadres internationaux tels que le Cadre mondial de la biodiversité de Kunming-Montréal, le Protocole sur les gaz à effet de serre (GHG Protocol) et les mécanismes de certification carbone (Verra, Gold Standard, etc.) imposent une prise en compte croissante des impacts climatiques et de la biodiversité dans la conception, l'évaluation et le suivi des projets de développement.

En Guinée, plusieurs projets miniers, énergétiques, agricoles et d'infrastructures sont désormais confrontés à ces nouvelles exigences, notamment en matière de comptabilisation des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, de séquestration du carbone, de restauration des écosystèmes et de compensation des impacts résiduels sur la biodiversité. Cette évolution nécessite un renforcement des capacités techniques des cadres de l'AGEE afin qu'ils puissent analyser de manière critique les études environnementales intégrant ces nouvelles dimensions, apprécier la pertinence des mesures proposées par les promoteurs et formuler des recommandations conformes aux meilleures pratiques internationales.

C'est dans cette perspective, et avec l'appui du Projet de Gestion des Ressources Naturelles, Mines et Environnement (PGRNME), que l'AGEE envisage de recruter un consultant spécialisé chargé d'assurer une formation de haut niveau au profit de ses cadres.

2. Objectif Général

Renforcer les compétences des cadres de l'AGEE en matière d'intégration des enjeux liés au changement climatique, au crédit carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité dans les processus d'évaluation environnementale et sociale, conformément aux exigences nationales et aux standards internationaux. Ce renforcement vise également à conforter l’AGEE dans son rôle d’autorité nationale de référence, à étendre progressivement ces compétences à ses antennes régionales et à garantir que la valorisation des actifs carbone et biodiversité profite équitablement à l’État guinéen et aux communautés locales.

De manière spécifique, Il s’agit de :

  • Maîtriser les concepts, principes et mécanismes relatifs au changement climatique, à la séquestration du carbone, aux crédits carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité.
  • Comprendre les cadres juridique, institutionnel et normatif nationaux et internationaux régissant les marchés du carbone et les mécanismes de compensation écologique.
  • Renforcer leurs capacités d'analyse des Études d'Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES), des Évaluations Environnementales Stratégiques (EES), des Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES) et des autres instruments de sauvegarde intégrant les enjeux climatiques et de biodiversité.
  • Maîtriser les méthodes et outils de calcul des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, de séquestration du carbone et d'évaluation des compensations de biodiversité (calcul métrique).
  • Développer les compétences nécessaires pour évaluer la pertinence des mesures d'atténuation, de compensation écologique et de restauration proposées dans les projets de développement.
  • Vérifier la robustesse des mesures d’atténuation et de compensation proposées dans les EIES et les PGES, en s’assurant de l’application effective de la hiérarchie d’atténuation (éviter, réduire, restaurer, compenser), de l’adéquation des mesures à l’ampleur des impacts, de la quantification des impacts résiduels ainsi que — pour le carbone comme pour la biodiversité — de l’additionnalité, de la permanence, de l’équivalence écologique et de la mesurabilité du suivi.
  • Harmoniser les pratiques d'évaluation au sein de l'AGEE en élaborant des outils d'analyse (guides, check-lists et critères techniques) intégrant les dimensions climat, carbone et biodiversité.
  • Renforcer les capacités des cadres à formuler des avis techniques et des recommandations conformes aux exigences nationales et aux standards internationaux en matière de changement climatique et de biodiversité.
  • Amener les bureaux d'études à intégrer systématiquement les enjeux liés au changement climatique, au crédit carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité dans les rapports d'évaluation environnementale et sociale.
  • Contribuer au déploiement des compétences et des outils d’analyse au niveau des antennes régionales de l’AGEE, afin d’assurer une application homogène des exigences liées au climat, au carbone et à la biodiversité sur l’ensemble du territoire national.
  • Renforcer la capacité des cadres à apprécier les mécanismes de partage des bénéfices et à défendre les intérêts de l’État guinéen et des communautés locales dans les projets mobilisant des crédits carbone et des compensations de biodiversité.

3. RÉSULTATS ATTENDUS

À l'issue de la formation, les résultats suivants sont attendus :

  • Les cadres de l'AGEE maîtrisent les concepts fondamentaux relatifs au changement climatique, à la séquestration du carbone, aux crédits carbones et à la compensation de la biodiversité.
  • Les cadres de l'AGEE sont capables d'analyser les Études d'Impact Environnemental et Social (EIES), les Évaluations Environnementales Stratégiques (EES), les Plans de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale (PGES) et les autres instruments de sauvegarde en intégrant les enjeux climatiques et de biodiversité.
  • Les méthodes et outils de calcul des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, de séquestration du carbone et de compensation de la biodiversité (calcul métrique) sont maîtrisés et appliqués dans l'analyse des dossiers soumis à l'AGEE.
  • Les cadres de l'AGEE disposent d'outils techniques harmonisés (guides, check-lists et critères d'analyse) pour l'évaluation des composantes climat, carbone et biodiversité dans les projets de développement.
  • Les capacités de l'AGEE à formuler des avis techniques et des recommandations conformes aux exigences nationales et aux standards internationaux en matière de changement climatique et de biodiversité sont renforcées.
  • Les cadres de l’AGEE sont capables de vérifier la robustesse des mesures d’atténuation et de compensation présentées dans les EIES et les PGES (application de la hiérarchie d’atténuation, additionnalité, permanence, équivalence écologique, quantification des impacts résiduels et mesurabilité du suivi) et de formuler des réserves ou des demandes de compléments techniquement fondées.
  • Les bureaux d'études sont mieux orientés et accompagnés pour intégrer les enjeux liés au changement climatique, au crédit carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité dans les rapports d'évaluation environnementale et sociale.
  • Les compétences et les outils d’analyse sont progressivement déployés au sein des antennes régionales de l’AGEE, assurant une qualité d’évaluation homogène sur l’ensemble du territoire national.
  • Les cadres de l’AGEE sont en mesure d’apprécier les mécanismes de partage des bénéfices et de veiller à ce que la valorisation des actifs carbone et biodiversité profite équitablement à l’État guinéen et aux communautés locales.
  • Un rapport de formation comprenant les supports pédagogiques, les études de cas, les recommandations et une feuille de route pour l'intégration des enjeux climatiques et de biodiversité dans les procédures de l'AGEE est élaboré et validé.

4. METHODOLOGIE DE MISE EN OEUVRE

La mission sera conduite selon une approche participative, interactive et axée sur le renforcement des capacités pratiques des cadres de l'AGEE, au siège comme dans les antennes régionales. Elle combinera des exposés théoriques, des études de cas, des exercices pratiques, des travaux de groupe et des échanges d'expériences afin de favoriser une meilleure appropriation des concepts et des outils.

5. LIVRABLES

Le consultant produira les livrables suivants :

  1. Un rapport de démarrage présentant la compréhension des Termes de Référence, la méthodologie de travail, le programme détaillé de la formation, le calendrier d'exécution ainsi que les supports pédagogiques préliminaires.
  2. Les modules et supports de formation (présentations PowerPoint, notes techniques, documents de référence, études de cas et exercices pratiques) intégrant les enjeux liés au changement climatique, à la séquestration du carbone, au crédit carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité.
  3. Des outils méthodologiques destinés aux cadres de l'AGEE et à ses antennes régionales, notamment :
  • une grille d'analyse des EIES intégrant les enjeux climatiques et de biodiversité, structurée autour de critères de robustesse (application de la hiérarchie d’atténuation, quantification des impacts résiduels, additionnalité, permanence, équivalence écologique et mesurabilité du suivi) ;
  • une check-list d'évaluation des aspects liés au changement climatique, au crédit carbone et à la compensation écologique, permettant de statuer sur la robustesse et la conformité des mesures et d’exiger, le cas échéant, des compléments ;
  • des fiches techniques sur les principales méthodes de calcul des émissions de gaz à effet de serre, de séquestration du carbone et des métriques de compensation de la biodiversité.

 

  1. Les rapports d'évaluation des participants, comprenant les résultats des pré-tests et post-tests, l'analyse des acquis et l'évaluation de la satisfaction des participants.
  2. Le rapport général de la formation, comprenant :
    • le déroulement des travaux ;
    • la liste des participants ;
    • les principales communications ;
    • les résultats des travaux de groupe ;
    • les recommandations formulées ;
    • les enseignements tirés de la formation.
  3. Une feuille de route assortie d'un plan d'action pour l'intégration progressive des enjeux liés au changement climatique, au crédit carbone et à la compensation de la biodiversité dans les procédures, les outils et les pratiques d'évaluation environnementale et sociale de l'AGEE. Elle précise notamment les modalités de déploiement progressif de ces acquis et outils au niveau des antennes régionales de l’AGEE.
  4. Une base documentaire numérique, comprenant l'ensemble des supports de formation, les textes réglementaires, les normes internationales, les guides techniques et les références bibliographiques utilisées durant la mission.
  5. Une note stratégique sur le positionnement de la Guinée au regard des marchés du carbone et de la biodiversité, formulant des recommandations pour sécuriser les intérêts de l’État et des communautés locales et pour conforter l’AGEE dans son rôle d’autorité nationale de référence.

6. PROFILS

a. Qualifications académiques

Le Consultant devra être titulaire d'un diplôme de niveau Bac+5 (Master II ou équivalent) au minimum en sciences de l'environnement, écologie, foresterie, changement climatique, gestion des ressources naturelles, biodiversité, géographie, aménagement du territoire, ingénierie environnementale, économie de l'environnement ou dans tout autre domaine pertinent.

Un diplôme de Doctorat ou des certifications professionnelles en changement climatique, finance carbone, biodiversité ou évaluations environnementales constitueront un atout.

b. Expérience professionnelle générale

Le Consultant devra justifier :

SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

RECRUTEMENT D'UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL – EXPERT(E) EN FINANCEMENT INSTITUTIONNEL POUR LA RÉALISATION D'UNE ÉTUDE SUR LES MÉCANISMES DE FINANCEMENT PÉRENNE DE L'AGEE

AMI N°10/PGRNME/MEDD/CI/2026

            Date de fin : 08 Septembre 2026

1. CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

Créée par le Décret D/2022/0346/PRG/CNRD/SGG/AN du 25 juillet 2022, l’Agence Guinéenne d’Évaluations Environnementales (AGEE) est l’autorité administrative chargée de l’évaluation, de l’approbation et du suivi de la conformité environnementale et sociale des projets publics et privés sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Cette mission de régulateur environnemental et d’appui-conseil aux promoteurs est essentielle pour garantir la durabilité des investissements et le respect des engagements internationaux de la Guinée en matière de gestion des risques environnementaux et sociaux.

Depuis sa création, l’AGEE assure ses missions grâce à un panachage de ressources budgétaires publiques, de redevances perçues sur les dossiers d’évaluation et d’appuis techniques et financiers de partenaires internationaux (Banque mondiale, BAD, PNUD, GIZ, etc.). Or, cette structure de financement présente des fragilités structurelles :

  • La part des subventions de l'État est soumise aux fluctuations budgétaires nationales ;
  • Les redevances perçues, bien que constituant une source de recettes propre, peuvent se révéler irrégulières ou insuffisamment dimensionnées par rapport aux coûts réels des missions de contrôle et de suivi ;
  • Les financements des partenaires techniques et financiers sont par nature limités dans le temps et ne sauraient couvrir les charges récurrentes de fonctionnement.

Face à la croissance soutenue du nombre de projets à évaluer et à superviser (mines, infrastructures routières, énergétiques et agricoles) et compte tenu de l’exigence accrue des normes internationales (Cadre Environnemental et Social de la Banque mondiale, par exemple), l’AGEE a besoin d’asseoir son autonomie financière sur des bases solides, prévisibles et pérennes.

C’est dans ce contexte que l’AGEE envisage de recruter un expert financier pour l’accompagner dans la conception d’un mécanisme de financement durable, équilibré et juridiquement sécurisé.

II. OBJECTIFS DE LA MISSION

L’objectif général de la mission est de doter l’AGEE d’une stratégie de financement à long terme, réaliste et opérationnelle, lui garantissant les moyens de son fonctionnement et de ses missions régaliennes de manière autonome et durable.

De manière spécifique, l’étude devra :

  1. Analyser la structure de coûts actuelle et future de l’AGEE afin de déterminer le besoin de financement annuel réaliste (fonctionnement, investissement, missions de contrôle).
  2. Évaluer les sources de financement existantes, en identifiant leurs forces, leurs faiblesses, leur base légale et leur potentiel de maximisation.
  3. Proposer des sources et mécanismes de financement innovants et pérennes, adaptés au cadre juridique guinéen et aux bonnes pratiques internationales de financement d’agences publiques de régulation et d’évaluation.
  4. Élaborer une feuille de route détaillée pour la mise en œuvre du (des) mécanisme(s) retenu(s), y compris les modifications législatives, réglementaires et procédurales nécessaires.

III. ÉTENDUE DE LA MISSION ET TÂCHES SPÉCIFIQUES

Sous l'autorité du Directeur Général de l'AGEE, l'expert financier sera chargé des tâches suivantes :

A. Diagnostic financier approfondi de l’AGEE (Analyse de l’existant)

  • Reconstituer et analyser les budgets de l’AGEE sur les cinq dernières années : recettes (subvention État, redevances, dons) et dépenses (masse salariale, missions de terrain, études, investissements).
  • Établir un compte d’exploitation analytique des principales activités (instruction des études, suivi/conformité, formation, sensibilisation).
  • Projeter le besoin de financement sur une période de 10 ans (2027-2037), en intégrant des hypothèses d’évolution du volume de dossiers, de renforcement des effectifs, d’inflation et d’investissements numériques (digitalisation des procédures).

B. Analyse du cadre juridique et institutionnel du financement

  • Faire l'inventaire exhaustif des textes législatifs et réglementaires régissant les ressources financières de l’AGEE (loi de création, textes fixant les taux des redevances, circulaires budgétaires).
  • Analyser les marges de manœuvre juridiques pour la mise en place de mécanismes de financement dédiés (affectation de recettes, compte d’affectation spéciale, fonds fiduciaire, agence dotée de l’autonomie financière, etc.).
  • Évaluer le risque juridique et la soutenabilité administrative de chaque option.

C. Benchmarking et identification des meilleures options de financement pérenne

  • Réaliser un benchmarking des mécanismes de financement d’agences environnementales ou d’évaluation comparables en Afrique subsaharienne et dans d’autres régions (ex : modèle de redevance proportionnelle au coût du projet, fonds national de compensation, taxes affectées, etc.).
  • Étudier la faisabilité des options suivantes pour le cas guinéen :
    • Redevance proportionnelle au coût de l’investissement (ad valorem), indexée sur le coût réel de la supervision ;
    • Redevance annuelle de suivi de la conformité pour les projets en exploitation ;
    • Taxe parafiscale sur les secteurs extractifs ou les grands travaux ;
    • Fonds fiduciaire national pour l’environnement abondé par une part des recettes minières ;
    • Contrats de performance et de partenariat avec les grands opérateurs ;
    • Contribution de service public des partenaires techniques et financiers (modalités de co-financement des contrôles).
  • Analyser chaque option selon des critères de rendement financier, d’équité, d’acceptabilité politique, de stabilité à long terme et de simplicité administrative.

D. Conception du mécanisme cible et feuille de route

  • Formuler, en concertation avec la Direction Générale, un scénario de financement cible (pouvant combiner plusieurs sources) clairement argumenté.
  • Simuler les projections de recettes sur 10 ans pour le scénario retenu et démontrer sa capacité à couvrir les besoins identifiés.
  • Rédiger les propositions d’ajustements des textes législatifs et réglementaires nécessaires à la mise en œuvre du mécanisme (sous forme d’avant-projets d’articles).
  • Élaborer une feuille de route opérationnelle détaillée (2027-2031) avec des étapes claires, un chiffrage, les responsabilités et les indicateurs de succès.

IV. LIVRABLES ATTENDUS

L’expert devra produire les livrables suivants, soumis à l’approbation du Directeur Général de l’AGEE et, si pertinent, d’un comité de pilotage :

  1. Rapport de démarrage (10 jours après le début de la mission) :
    • Méthodologie détaillée, plan de travail actualisé, liste des parties prenantes à rencontrer, canevas des outils de collecte de données (financières et juridiques), contraintes identifiées.

 

  1. Rapport de diagnostic financier et juridique (au plus tard 45 jours après le démarrage) :
    • Analyse des budgets passés, projections des besoins 2027-2037.
    • Cartographie des contraintes et opportunités juridiques pour les nouveaux mécanismes de financement.
  1. Rapport d’étape sur les options de financement (au plus tard 75 jours après le démarrage) :
    • Rapport de benchmarking international;
    • Analyse comparative des options de financement, avec simulation de rendement pour chaque scénario réaliste.
  1. Rapport provisoire du mécanisme cible et feuille de route (au plus tard 100 jours après le démarrage) :
    • Scénario retenu avec simulation financière détaillée.
    • Propositions de textes juridiques.
    • Projet de feuille de route.
  1. Rapport final intégrant les observations de l’AGEE et de l’atelier de validation (au plus tard 15 jours après réception des commentaires de l’Agence sur le rapport provisoire) :
    • Synthèse exécutive prête à être présentée au Conseil d’Administration de l’AGEE, au Ministère de tutelle et aux partenaires techniques et financiers.

Le rapport provisoire devra être présenté lors d’un atelier de validation à Conakry avec les parties prenantes nationales.

V. DURÉE, LIEU ET CALENDRIER DE LA MISSION

  • La durée prévisionnelle d’exécution de toute la mission est de 90 jours-homme (calendaires), répartis sur une période maximale de 5 mois incluant les délais d’examen et de validation des livrables.
  • Calendrier indicatif :
    • Phase 1 (Diagnostic): Mois 1 et 2.
    • Phase 2 (Benchmarking & Options) : Mois 3.
    • Phase 3 (Scénario cible & Feuille de route) : Mois 4.
    • Phase 4 (Finalisation & Restitution) : Mois 5.
  • Lieu d’affectation : Conakry, dans les locaux de l’AGEE, avec une réunion de cadrage et des entretiens avec les ministères (Environnement, Finances, Budget, Mines) et les partenaires techniques et financiers. Une ou plusieurs missions à l’intérieur du pays ne sont pas à exclure si des projets pilotes de financement régional sont à documenter.

VI. QUALIFICATIONS ET EXPÉRIENCE REQUISES

Le/la consultant(e) devra justifier des qualifications suivantes :

  • Diplôme universitaire de niveau Bac+5 minimum (Master, DESS, DEA, Ingénieur) en finances publiques, économie, gestion financière, droit des finances publiques, audit ou domaine connexe ;
  • Une spécialisation supplémentaire en économie de l’environnement ou en gestion institutionnelle serait un atout appréciable ;
  • Expérience professionnelle d’au moins 10 ans dans le conseil en financement institutionnel et en finances publiques,
  • Avoir deux (2) expériences justifiées dans la conception ou l’évaluation de mécanismes de financement d’établissements publics, d’agences de régulation ou de fonds fiduciaires ;
  • Solide connaissance du cadre juridique guinéen des finances publiques (LOLF, Code des Marchés Publics, régimes de taxes parafiscales, comptes d’affectation spéciale) et des procédures budgétaires de l’État ;
  • Connaissance du fonctionnement des agences environnementales ou d’institutions similaires en Afrique de l’Ouest en général ou en Guinée plus particulière constituerait un atout ;
  • Excellentes capacités de modélisation financière sur tableur (Excel) et de rédaction de textes juridiques simples et opérationnels ;
  • Maîtrise parfaite du français à l'écrit et à l'oral.

VII. QUALITÉS PERSONNELLES ET COMPÉTENCES TRANSVERSALES

  • Capacité d’écoute et de dialogue avec des interlocuteurs variés (direction générale, ministères, bailleurs de fonds, secteur privé).
  • Rigueur analytique, force de proposition et pragmatisme.
  • Capacité à faire preuve de diplomatie et de discrétion professionnelle sur des sujets budgétaires sensibles.

VIII. SUPERVISION ET REPORTING

Le Consultant travaillera sous la supervision directe du Directeur Général de l’AGEE. Pour le suivi quotidien et la coordination technique, un point focal sera désigné au sein de l’Agence (ex : Service Administratif et Financier ou responsable du suivi des programmes).

Le consultant présentera mensuellement l’état d’avancement de son travail au comité de pilotage de l’étude, qui pourra être composé de cadres de l’AGEE, d’un représentant du Ministère en charge des Finances et d’un représentant des partenaires techniques et financiers.

Tous les livrables devront être validés par ce comité avant d’être considérés comme définitifs.

IX. METHODE DE SÉLECTION

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

GEORGIA

Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land Project (GRAIL) – P175629

Loan No. 9504-GE 

Assignment title: Consulting Services for the Development of an Institutional Strengthening Strategy, Roadmap, and Action Plan for Sustainable Agricultural Land Management in Georgia

 

Reference No. GR/CS/CQS/15

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Georgia Resilient Agriculture, Irrigation and Land (GRAIL) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The project cost is USD 150.00 million comprising of an equal share of USD 75.00 million by each co-financer.

The project development objectives are to: (a) improve irrigation, and drainage services, and agricultural production in project areas; and (b) strengthen national irrigation and land management institutional capacity for climate resilient planning. The primary project beneficiaries comprise farmers and agricultural enterprises across the project targeted regions. Overall, the rural population will benefit from enhanced services provided by land management, irrigation services, and agricultural support. In the public sector, the project will support institutional strengthening of Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture (MEPA), including Georgian Amelioration (GA), Rural Development Agency (RDA) and Land Management Agency (LMA). The Project consists of the following two main components: Component 1. Resilient Irrigated Agriculture and Component 2: Improved Land Management Capacity.

To ensure the long-term sustainability of agricultural resources, the Government seeks to strengthen the institutional framework and develop a clear roadmap supporting sustainable land management (SLM). Therefore, this assignment is designed to provide the technical assistance necessary to assess existing capacities and establish a robust Institutional Strategy and Action Plan for the LMA and relevant MEPA departments, specifically the Hydro-melioration and Land Management Department (MLMD) of MEPA.

The overarching goal of the assignment is to guide the strategic, technical, and institutional empowerment of the LMA and the MLMD of MEPA, ensuring they can effectively execute their statutory responsibilities through modern, data-driven frameworks. The primary objective of the Institutional Strengthening Strategy and the accompanying 5-year strategic roadmap is to provide MEPA and the LMA with a comprehensive, evidence-based blueprint for institutional modernization. Rather than dictating immediate technical execution, these strategic deliverables will be designed to logically sequence necessary administrative reforms, optimize business processes and align with statutory land management mandates, establish the conceptual prerequisites for future digital transformation, and define a clear, costed path for long-term operational and financial sustainability. Rather than redefining mandates already set by their statutes, the Strategy and Action Plan will structure and phase interventions across four core components:

  • Institutional Strategy: Defining what the entities do, how they are optimally structured, and how they are financially sustained;
  • Business Processes: Mapping and reengineering how they operate internally and exchange data with external registries and agencies;
  • Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) Strategy & Enterprise Architecture: Defining the specific technology architecture, readiness parameters, and priority use cases that enable those business processes;
  • Data Architecture: Modeling conceptual target data environments, metadata rules or instructions, and operational data flows;

 

Key objectives include:

  • land management to identify specific gaps and opportunities for technical and administrative reform, and to translate existing legal mandates into clear, efficient technical workflows and administrative business processes for both entities;
  • Develop targeted recommendations and proposals to support the harmonization of land-related legislation with broader environmental and agricultural policies, aimed at fostering a coherent legal framework for sustainable land use;
  • Conduct a comprehensive capacity assessment and develop a Strategy for the Institutional Development of the LMA and relevant MEPA structures (specifically the MLMD), focused on strengthening their ability to fulfill statutory responsibilities that will include the proposed optimized organizational setups, human resource strategies, and staffing models tailored to support modernized workflows of the entities;
  • Formulate Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and explicit operational plans for specialized land management mandates. This includes: (i) the planning, restoration, rehabilitation, and landscape-level cultivation of windbreaks; (ii) the national pasture inventory program and sustainable management practices; and (iii) monitoring, supervision, and regulatory compliance workflows for topsoil preservation and management - all in accordance with existing legislation and the forthcoming Law on Sustainable Pasture Management;
  • Explore Advanced Land Monitoring and Remote Sensing Feasibility: Conduct a comprehensive assessment of the practical operational requirements, data readiness, technical infrastructure constraints, and user needs to conceptually integrate modernized LCLU monitoring and automated crop identification use cases leveraging satellite data (e.g., Sentinel) and relevant geoprocessing tasks into daily workflows, and detail integration into the strategic roadmap. This shall include a rigorous evaluation of international standards (such as FAO, EU INSPIRE, or IPCC) and relevant country best practices to define, justify, and adapt the technical and methodological frameworks required to institutionalize continuous, evidence-based land monitoring tailored to Georgian operational requirements;
  • Develop a comprehensive 5-year public finance model to support recurring expenses for IT infrastructure, system asset maintenance, data procurement pipelines, and technical staff development across both entities;
  • Provide a comprehensive capacity building framework, including a detailed training-of-trainers (ToT) curriculum and technical user guides, ensuring that staff within the LMA and MLMD possess the internal capacity required to manage the strategy and roadmap independently.

Indicative assignment duration: The duration of the assignment is estimated at twelve (12) months from the date of contract signature.

The Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture of Georgia (MEPA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Expression of interest should cover, but not limited to: corporate profile, years in business, experience relevant to the project activities, overall key staff resources, and core business.

The selection criteria are:

The Consultant shall be a firm/consortium with demonstrated experience in:

  • Institutional Expertise: A minimum of 10 years of experience in institutional reform, land management policy, and public sector governance, including the development of national-level land management strategies and action plans;
  • Specialized SLM Expertise: Proven track record and a multidisciplinary pool of specialists with documented expertise across the key thematic areas of Sustainable Land Management (SLM) as relevant to the scope and objectives of this assignment;
  • Business Process & Conceptual Systems Architecture Capability: Documented corporate experience in large-scale Business Process Reengineering (BPR), conceptual data modeling, and systems integration planning within public administration or land sectors;

Assignment Title: Consulting Services for Feasibility Study and Preliminary Design of Ulaanbaatar - Mandalgovi Road Reconstruction Project

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): ZTYa/20260804057

 

The Government of Mongolia has received a grant financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), through the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP), under Grant No. TF0D0692 to support the preparation of the Gobi Connectivity Improvement Project. The objective of the grant is to facilitate the preparation of a proposed project designed to enhance the efficiency, safety, and climate resilience of transport along the Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi road corridor, while strengthening institutional capacity for its sustainable maintenance.

 

The Ulaanbaatar–Mandalgovi (A0201) corridor is a nationally significant transport artery that forms a central spine in Mongolia’s north–south mobility network. Stretching approximately 272km, the corridor links Ulaanbaatar with the aimag centers of Tuv and Dundgobi while providing a gateway to southern regions with economies shaped by livestock, mining, tourism, and services. The road is also an important feeder into broader regional transport and trade corridors, including routes serving large scale mining operations and cross border freight movements.

 

Originally constructed in 2012–2013 to Asian Highway ClassIII standards, the existing two-lane road has reached a critical stage of deterioration. The corridor’s geometric design, originally intended for lower traffic volumes and slower heavy vehicle growth, no longer aligns with current or projected operational demands.

 

In response to these factors, the Ministry of Road and Transport (MRT) seeks a comprehensive feasibility assessment, including the preparation of preliminary design, that evaluates the potential of upgrading the A0201 corridor to a fourlane Class I standard. This upgrade would enhance freight fluidity, reduce travel times, strengthen supply chain reliability, and improve road safety outcomes. In line with the Government of Mongolia’s Action Plan for 2024–2028, which sets the objective of initiating the fourlane expansion of this corridor, the assessment and preliminary design will serve as the analytical backbone for subsequent safeguard instruments, procurement strategies, and engineering design stages, ensuring that the reconstruction approach is fit for purpose, fiscally prudent, and environmentally and socially responsible.

As a crosscutting requirement, the assignment will also encompass environmental and social due diligence tasks, including screening against the World Bank's Environmental and Social Standards (ESS1–ESS10), preparation of the Environmental and Social Management Plan (PESMP), and inputs into subsequent safeguard instruments such as a Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM), in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

Qualificação Requerida da Consultoria

A consultoria deverá apresentar experiência em:

i.     Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) trabalhos concluídos nos últimos 10 (dez) anos, relacionados aos seguintes temas: identificação e mapeamento de áreas com aptidão para restauração florestal ou para regeneração da vegetação natural preferencialmente na Amazônia; implantação, fortalecimento e monitoramento de sistemas produtivos, sistemas agroflorestais, restauração de florestal, agricultura regenerativa, monitoramento da restauração na preferencialmente na Amazônia, mapeamento participativo em territórios quilombolas e outras comunidades tradicionais.

ii.     Execução de, no mínimo, 5 (cinco) contratos, projetos ou serviçosno desenvolvimento de, diagnósticos socioeconômicos e ambientais, desenvolvimento de sistemas agroflorestais, agricultura regenerativa, regeneração da vegetação nativa preferencialmente no estado do Pará e/ou em outras áreas com reconhecimento de gestão integrada na Amazônia.

iii.    Execução de, no mínimo, 3 (três) contratos, projetos ou serviços  de gestão ambiental e territorial com mapeamento participativo em áreas rurais de comunidades agricultoras, extrativistas, quilombolas ou indígenas, preferencialmente na Amazônia.

A consultoria deverá demonstrar capacidade técnica para planejar e executar pesquisas de campo em múltiplos territórios; produzir análises socioeconômicas, ambientais e institucionais; operar ferramentas de georreferenciamento e sistemas de informação geográfica (SIG); elaborar bancos de dados e indicadores de monitoramento e produzir relatórios técnicos, mapas temáticos e documentos analíticos.

 

A equipe chave deverá contar com os seguintes profissionais:  1 Coordenador(a)-Geral e 1 Especialista em Gestão Territorial e Ambiental . A consultoria deverá designar equipe de apoio necessária para realização das atividades desse TDR, sendo sugerida a inclusão de um técnico para atuar em campo.

 

            As Manifestações de Interesse deverão ser enviadas até dia 10/09/2026, às 23:59 horas, para o e-mail  asl2.compras@fgv.br. AVIS À MANIFESTATION D'INTÉRÊT

« SÉLECTION D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL NATIONAL POUR L’ÉVALUATION DES POINTS D’ENTRÉE (PoE) ET DES CENTRES DE SURVEILLANCE ÉPIDÉMIOLOGIQUE (CSE) »

 

  1. Contexte

 Le Gouvernement de la République du Tchad, à travers le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention, bénéficie de l’appui financier de la Banque mondiale pour la mise en œuvre du Projet [nom du Projet].

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet, il est prévu de renforcer les capacités nationales de prévention, de détection et de réponse aux menaces sanitaires, notamment à travers l’amélioration des capacités de surveillance épidémiologique et des capacités requises au niveau des Points d’Entrée (PoE), conformément aux exigences du Règlement sanitaire international (RSI, 2005).

À cet effet, le Projet envisage de recruter un Consultant Individuel National chargé de réaliser une évaluation exhaustive des capacités des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE).

  1. Objet de la mission

La mission consiste à réaliser une évaluation détaillée et documentée des capacités de l’ensemble des Points d’Entrée (PoE) et des Centres de Surveillance Épidémiologique (CSE) concernés, afin d’identifier les capacités existantes, les insuffisances, les écarts par rapport aux exigences applicables, ainsi que les besoins prioritaires de renforcement.

Le consultant devra notamment effectuer des visites physiques sur l’ensemble des sites concernés et produire un rapport d’évaluation assorti d’un plan d’amélioration opérationnel et priorisé.

  1. Profil et qualifications requis

Le consultant devra notamment répondre aux exigences suivantes :

  • être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en santé publique, épidémiologie, médecine, santé internationale ou dans un domaine directement pertinent ;
  • justifier d’au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans les systèmes de surveillance épidémiologique ;
  • disposer d’une expérience avérée dans l’évaluation des systèmes de surveillance et/ou des systèmes de santé ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans l’évaluation des capacités sanitaires des Points d’Entrée (PoE) ;
  • avoir une excellente connaissance du RSI (2005) ;
  • avoir une bonne maîtrise de la Surveillance Intégrée de la Maladie et la Riposte (SIMR) ;
  • disposer d’une expérience dans la préparation et la réponse aux urgences de santé publique ;
  • avoir une bonne capacité de collecte, de traitement et d’analyse des données ;
  • disposer d’excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et analytiques en français ;
  • maîtriser les outils bureautiques et les outils d’analyse et de traitement des données ;
  • avoir une bonne connaissance du contexte du système de santé et du dispositif national de surveillance épidémiologique du Tchad.
  • Une expérience de travail avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Prévention et/ou les structures nationales de surveillance constituera un avantage.
  1. Durée de la mission

La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours calendaires.

La mission nécessitera des déplacements à N’Djaména ainsi que dans les provinces et localités où sont implantés les PoE et les CSE concernés par l’évaluation.

5. Méthode de sélection

Le consultant sera recruté conformément aux dispositions du Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant un Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition septembre 2025, selon la méthode de Sélection de Consultants Individuels (CI).

Assignment Title: Consulting services for the preparation of preliminary design, tender documentation and evaluation of bids in the selection of a Contractor for the construction of the 110 kV overhead line between the Lower Tar HPP and the "Kara-Kulja" Substation

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan) KG/KRED/CS/2026/CQS-01

The Kyrgyz Republic has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Kyrgyz Renewable Energy Development Project (KRED) – Phase 1 and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the preparation of the preliminary design and tender documentation, and support in the evaluation of bids for the construction of the 110 kV overhead transmission line between the Lower Tar HPP and the Kara-Kulja Substation.

Under Component 1 of the KRED Project, a new 110 kV overhead transmission line of approximately 18 km is envisaged to connect the 19 MW Lower Tar Small HPP, located in Kara-Kulja District, Osh Region, to the existing 110 kV Kara-Kulja Substation. The services are expected to commence in Q4 2026. Approximately five (5) months are envisaged for completion of the preliminary design and tender documentation. The contract will be lump sum.

NATIONAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT FINANCE COMMITTEE

                      Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project – GESD 2.0

                                                  Agreement No:  IDA-E6540

Individual Consultant- Project Engineer (2)

No: MW-NLGFC-563895-CS-INDIV/ MW-NLGFC-563897-CS-INDIV

                     

                                          Date of Issue: 20th August ,2026

  1. Background

 

The Government of Malawi (GoM) through the National Local Government Finance Committee (NLGFC) has received financing towards the cost of Governance to Enable Service Delivery (GESD) Project. The NLGFC intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring two Project Engineer on a three - year contract renewable annually based on performance and availability of financial resources or mutually agreed by both parties.    

 

NLGFC therefore invites applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position of two (2) Project Engineer tenable at the NLGFC Offices. The terms of Reference (TORs) for two (2) Project Engineer) are as follows:

 

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

The Project Engineer (Specialist) shall lead, coordinate and support local authorities and all relevant ministries, departments and agencies in the design and implementation of the project. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will lead and have approving authority for preparing and/or interpreting designs, bill of quantities (BoQs), tendering and engineering cost estimates prepared. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will work closely with relevant district authorities, including district engineers, other officers and specialists in the PIT, including safeguards, Project Coordinator, NLGFC, MoLGRD and other relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to supervision consultants. The Project Engineer (Specialist) will support monitoring of the sub-projects and will address and manage technical engineering questions in local investment projects implemented by the local authorities that are financed by GESD 2.0. 

 

  1. Duties and Responsibilities of the Project Engineer (Consultant)

 

The Project Engineers (Consultants) will be responsible for providing technical leadership and engineering oversight to ensure that project activities are planned, designed, implemented, monitored, and completed in accordance with approved specifications, quality standards, budget, schedule, and applicable regulations.

 

Specific tasks will include the following:

 

  1. Coordinate and support all engineering functions and activities related to infrastructure construction and rehabilitation in the local authorities, namely Department of Planning and Development and Department of Public Works;
  2. Support data collection for all proposed sub-project sites to aid development and customisation of architectural designs, production of BoQs and engineering estimates, tendering processes and ensuring that designs are in conformity with results of site-specific resilience and risk related investigations and analysis;
  3. Ensure timely and correct submission of information into the Public Management Information System (PMIS) by local authorities;
  4. Provide technical support to the Local Authorities in project selection, reviewing annual investment plans, works designs, BoQs, costs estimate, tendering, supervision and monitoring;
  5. Coordinate topographic surveys for the design of infrastructure to be developed under the Project;
  6. Support local authorities in conducting initial site investigation;
  7. Facilitate the production of location maps and sketches if necessary for all engineering sites that need maintenance and repair (selected as subprojects under GESD 2.0);
  8. Support and if necessary lead the review and approval of submissions by design engineers, including ensuring timely submission of the same;
  9. Support and if necessary lead design options stakeholder consultations with communities and relevant departments so that their inputs are incorporated in the designs to ensure acceptance and ownership of solutions to be developed;
  10. Conduct technical supervision of all construction works ensuring that the works are implemented to the required standards, within the assigned cost and time;
  11. Check Supervision Consultant’s work so as to conduct verification of contractors’ payment claims for works done;
  12. Manage changes to engineering constructions works ensuring that any changes have no adverse effect on the project and they are undertaken following project works change protocols, including documentation;
  13. Facilitate preparation of work plans and budgets for local investment projects to ensure relevance to outputs and outcomes of local investment project;
  14. Support the preparation of schedule of works and materials for project activities in collaboration with relevant stakeholders;
  15. Review and assess contractors’ and consultants’ payment certificates for engineering works
  16. Prepare and conduct training programs for Local Authority technical staff involved in contract and procurement management; and other related activities as directed by the PIT;
  17. Ensure compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements;
  18. Liaise with other project specialists and officers, including safeguards, occupational health & safety, procurement, and advise the PIT on all construction Engineering technical related matters;
  19. Collect projects’ progress reports from the LAs, liaise with the monitoring & evaluation officer in the PIT in producing reports for project activities, consolidate them and submit them to PIT/PC, Executive Director and World Bank Task Team;
  20. Preparation and timely submission of monthly, quarterly and annual engineering project progress reports and other reports to the Project Coordinator, Executive Director and the World Bank Task Team.
  21. Facilitating the review of Annual Investment Plans (AIPs) for Local authorities and provide guidance on cost and time estimates.

 

  1. Deliverables

 

Deliverables for the assignment correspond to the duties and responsibilities above. Specifically, they will comprise:

 

  1. Timely review of AIPs submitted by local authorities, including review of cost and time estimates;
  2. Reviewed and approved engineering designs and drawings.
  3. Technical specifications and BoQs.
  4. Engineering project progress reports and other reports timely compiled
  5. Site inspection reports.
  6. Quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) reports.
  7. Defects and corrective action reports.
  8. Monthly and quarterly progress reports, aligned with PMIS information.
  9. Physical progress monitoring reports.
  10. Work completion certificates.

 

  1. Performance Criteria

 

The following performance criteria will be used to assess the performance of the Project Engineer annually and based upon these assessments the contract with the project (GESD 2.0) may be continued or terminated:

  • 100% of required technical reports submitted on time.
  • At least 95% compliance with approved engineering specifications and quality standards.
  • Site inspections conducted according to approved supervision schedules.
  • 100% of contractor payment certificates reviewed and processed within agreed timelines.
  • All identified defects and non-compliance issues addressed within specified corrective action periods.
  • Minimal cost and schedule overruns attributable to technical deficiencies.
  • No major engineering failures or quality-related incidents.
  • Timely completion and handover of project infrastructure.
  • PMIS utilization by local authorities.

 

  1. Qualifications, Skills and Expertise

 

The candidate should meet the following minimum qualifications:

 

  1. Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering/Architecture/Quantity Surveying
  2. Master’s Degree in Construction/Engineering related field and ;
  3. Registration with an approved professional body, such as Malawi Engineering Institution/Board of Architects and Quantity Surveyors
  4. A minimum of 8 years of relevant working experience;
  5. Excellent communications, writing/reporting skills;
  6. Proficiency in computer aided design packages (AutoCAD, ArchCAD, GIS etc)
  7. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Microsoft Project etc.);
  8. Strong organizational, self-starting and communications skills;
  9. Experience working with government institutions and organizations; working experience with local authorities in Malawi is considered an advantage;
  10. Highly motivated and enthusiastic person with excellent planning, analytical, communications and interpersonal skills as well as a high level of diplomacy; and
  11. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, as well as team participation and management skills

 

  1. Reporting Arrangements

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will primarily report to the Project Coordinator with a technical reporting line to the Director of Social and Economic Services at NLGFC for all technical matters, and will support local authorities’ in implementation of GESD 2.0 project.

 

  1. Location of Assignment

 

The Project Engineer (Specialist) will be based at the NLGFC offices in Lilongwe. The Project Engineer (Consultant) will occasionally be required to travel to local government authorities in Malawi where the Project is implementing its activities to engage with district officials to guide and improve project implementation.

 

  1. Duration of Assignment

 

The assignment is expected to span a total period of up to three (3) years, with annual performance reviews and contract extensions subject to satisfactory performance.

Assignment Title: Framework Agreements for the Preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMP), and Environmental and Social Audits (ESA).

 

The Lebanese Republic (hereinafter called the “Borrower”) has received financing in the amount of US$250 million from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (the “Bank”) toward the cost of the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), acting as the executing agency on behalf of the Government of Lebanon, intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under contracts for consulting services under Framework Agreements.

The consulting services (“the Services”) involve engaging qualified Environmental and Social consulting firms under Framework Agreements to provide environmental and social assessment services, including the preparation of Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), and Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs), for infrastructure and public service projects financed under the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP). The Framework Agreements will be concluded through a Two-Stage Selection Process and the consulting services shall include the preparation of:

  • Module 1: Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP) Checklist (Low-Risk Subprojects);
  • Module 2: Site-Specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs);
  • Module 3: Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs), including Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs);
  • Module 4: Environmental and Social Audits (ESAs), including Environmental and Social Action Plans (ESAPs) for Existing Facilities.

Specific Call-Off Contracts will be issued, on an as-needed basis, depending on the environmental and social risk classification of each activity in accordance with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF). The Framework Agreement(s) shall be signed for a duration of Thirty-Six (36) months with one or more qualified consulting firms. Individual assignments shall subsequently be awarded through Call-Off competitions among Framework Agreement holders.

The full version of the Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found on the CDR website at: https://www.cdr.gov.lb/Procurement.

Method: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)

 

  1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performance indicator values into color-coded risk flags for display in the executive dashboard. Task 3: Technical Assistance (TA) and Capacity Building: Develop and deliver a structured, tiered capacity-building programme and associated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. Task 4: Sustainable Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Model for the Gateway: Assess the technical and operational requirements for sustained operation of the Gateway, including hosting, security, data management, updates, user support and maintenance schedules and prepare indicative annual cost projections for the post-project period. Task 5: Envisaged functionality of the Africa RISE Gateway: The Africa RISE Gateway, as a go-to information and knowledge solution, is envisaged to serve.
