1. Introduction & Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau & Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

Energy Fiji Ltd (EFL) operates a National Control Centre in Vuda Back Road, Nadi  on the North-Western side of Vitilevu which is responsible for real-time monitoring and control of the national electricity grid. As demand grows, and renewable energy integration increases, the current NCC infrastructure and operational procedures require assessment to ensure efficiency, security, and reliability are not compromised and are operating well in optimum conditions.

1.1    The Renewable Energy Implementation Journey

EFL is currently embarking on a Renewable Energy Implementation Journey mainly focused on Variable Renewable Energy Sources (VRES) particularly, hydro, solar and wind which is intended over the next ten (10) years, majority of it will be solar.

  • Grid Demand Current demand for main VLIS grid currently sits at over 213MW which is expected to rise to over 300MW in the next ten years. As per the current Renewable Energy Roadmap,
  • Target Capacity: Under the current Renewable Energy Roadmap, EFL aims to install 165MW of solar capacity alongside 40MW+ of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) over the next 5 years

Modernized equipment is vital to ensure continuous forecasting, real-time grid stabilization, voltage management, and optimal battery dispatch to protect power grid inertia and prevent blackouts.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to identify technical, operational, and structural gaps between the NCC’s current capabilities and the required "future state". The future state must support a modern, secure grid running on 90% or more renewable energy as per EFL's national targets

3. Scope of Work

The selected consultant will complete the following tasks: 

  • Assessing current SCADA/EMS infrastructure.
  • Evaluating grid security and stability management practices.
  • Reviewing operational procedures, cybersecurity, and staffing availability & competence.
  • Providing a detailed roadmap to bridge identified gaps with an associated cost to carry this out – detailed list of hardware and software requirements, and required capacity for EFL (staffing and required certification)
  • Supporting EFL to define an appropriate procurement strategy and draft the procurement documents. The consultant will assess the available procurement options and recommend a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy, including packaging and contract type, based on the future-state architecture, market analysis and allocation of implementation risks. The appropriate bidding documents should then be prepared on the basis of the agreed strategy.

 

To complete above tasks, the consultant shall perform a comprehensive, multi-dimensional assessment covering the following areas:

 

3.1. Technical Infrastructure (SCADA/EMS/IT)

  • Review the age, reliability, and functional capacity of the current SCADA/Energy Management System (EMS).
  • Generator-side response performance, including whether or not it is automated.
  • Review existing data acquisition, data management, and analytics capabilities of the NCC, including the definition of future-state data and analytics requirements to support advanced EMS functions, operator situational awareness, and grid modernization.
  • Analyze communication infrastructure (telemetry, fiber optics, backup systems).
  • Assess integration capabilities for new technologies (smart grid, renewable energy management). 
  • Test for latency, signal loss, and failover readiness across fiber or microwave networks to ensure optimum communication links.

 

3.2. Operational Processes, Procedures & Readiness

  • Evaluate operating procedures (SOPs) for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Evaluate supply and demand management, including demand forecasts and generation forecasts, for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Assess grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability).
  • Analyse compliance with grid codes and regulatory frameworks not only locally but to align to international standards and best practices
  • Analyze the center's ability to manage intermittent distributed energy resources (DERs) and low-inertia systems
  • Review automatic voltage regulation (AVR) and load frequency control (LFC) performance
  • Assess existing disaster recovery and black-start coordination procedures.
  • Identify state of the art weather forecasting tools to optimise generation mix in favour of our hydros and solar PVs

 

3.3. Cybersecurity & Physical Security

  • Review cybersecurity protocols for Operational Technology (OT) and IT infrastructure.
  • Assess physical security of the main NCC and disaster recovery/backup control center. 

Audit compliance with Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards, including electronic security perimeters and access controls

 

3.4. Human Resources & Competence

  • Assess staffing levels, skill sets, and training programs for operators and engineers.
  • Evaluate human factors, control room ergonomics, and mental workload. 
  •  Identify gaps in national energy policies or grid codes that hinder modern operations.
  • Evaluate the technical competency of operators in handling advanced grid planning and simulation tools.

 

3.5. Environmental & Social Safeguards

  • Assess current energy use, and waste management practices at NCC and
  • Evaluate energy-efficient technologies, waste reduction strategies and sustainable procurement practices aligned with Fiji’s National laws and Good International Industry Practice.
  • Assess infrastructure capacity for adequate disability inclusion and gender-based rest rooms/ablution facility.

4. Methodology

The consultant is expected to carry out the following as part of the Gap Analysis:

  1. Conduct Desktop Review: Review existing documentation (grid codes, annual reports, previous audits, processes & procedures).
  2. Stakeholder Consultations: Conduct interviews with NCC operators, management, IT, Telecom/SCADA staff.
  3. Site Visits: Perform physical inspection of the control room, hardware, and backup facilities.
  4. Review of current Grid Code
  5. Benchmarking: Compare findings against international best practices (e.g., IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E).

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Empowered Green Pest Control Technology for Cowpea (Contract No.: GDCS-019) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on AI-empowered green pest control technology for cowpea.

I.Background

Cowpea is a major vegetable crop; however, pests such as thrips are particularly difficult to control during its cultivation. These pests can cause severe damage, including blackened heads and tails, insect holes, pod wrapping, and pod rot. Unscientific and non-standard pest control measures can easily lead to safety hazards, making cowpea pesticide residue a key focus of monitoring.

Traditional control methods for thrips heavily rely on pesticide spraying. However, the outer layer of cowpea flowers is tightly closed, while the inner layer is pouch-like, providing a natural "shelter" for thrips. No matter how the pesticides are sprayed, it is difficult to completely eliminate the pests hidden inside the flowers, failing to achieve ideal control results. Furthermore, irregular use of pesticides increases the risk of residue. Thrips are most active at temperatures of around 25°C, with peak activity typically occurring between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM. Their population dynamics and occurrence across different cowpea growth stages are closely related to climatic conditions.

Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—such as AI, drones, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to monitor the cowpea cultivation process and enable quality traceability, thereby achieving full-chain safety management from production to distribution.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

1.Guided by the goal of enhancing food safety, accurately predict key meteorological factors and other variables during the cowpea cultivation process to provide data support for large-scale cowpea planting management, thereby effectively boosting the efficiency of high-quality agricultural development.

2.Research and develop an integrated agricultural cultivation and management service model for cowpea production that covers pre-risk early warning, in-process risk control, and post-risk resolution, standardizing the full-chain safe production management process "from farm to table." Based on the actual requirements for the sustainable development of cowpea production, cultivation management processes, and product standards, establish a green pest control technology model that is adaptable to practical production and suitable for widespread promotion.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies in cowpea production, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI. Taking into account the actual conditions of domestic cowpea-producing regions, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of a "Low-Altitude + Meteorological + Sensor" Early Warning Model for Cowpea Growth and Pest/Disease Risks

Develop an information model for cowpea growth anomalies by modeling the nonlinear relationships between various meteorological factors and crop growth status across different growth stages. Based on high-resolution agricultural meteorological data from satellite remote sensing, and combined with ground sensor data monitoring temperature, humidity, light, rainfall, and soil moisture, quantitatively analyze and predict the risks to cowpea growth caused by abnormal climatic conditions—such as drought, low temperatures, and high temperatures—over large-scale planting areas for the next 7 to 15 days.

Furthermore, as thrips are currently the primary pest threatening cowpeas, with an optimal activity temperature of approximately 25°C and specific occurrence patterns across different growth stages, a quantitative database for crop pest and disease risks will be established. This involves modeling the risk probability of pest and disease proliferation based on different cowpea phenotypes under varying meteorological conditions. Integrated with large-scale crop growth stage estimation technology, this system will analyze the occurrence probability of major pests and diseases, such as thrips, thereby enabling proactive prevention.

3. Research and Application of Intelligent Crop Monitoring and Precision Fertilizer & Pesticide Management Technologies for Cowpea Cultivation

Based on the application research of systems including precision agricultural meteorological forecasts, crop growth estimation models, and risk early-warning models, this task aims to develop and demonstrate a precision pesticide application technology system integrating pest monitoring with fertigation (water and fertilizer integration). The study will apply efficient UAV-based pest monitoring technology to achieve early detection of pests and diseases, and conduct research on adjusting water and fertilizer agronomic practices and pesticide management based on the risk early-warning models. Demonstration bases will be established to continuously track and monitor the effectiveness of pest control and eradication through technology integration. The study will evaluate the pesticide reduction effects and cowpea compliance rates, and formulate standard operating procedures (SOPs) for precision management in cowpea production.

4.Exploring Adaptable Technologies and Establishing Screening Mechanisms Centered on Core Green Pest Control Issues for Cowpea

Intelligent Pest Monitoring Technology: Develop an intelligent pest monitoring system combining trapping with AI image recognition. This system is based on a deep vision pest identification system and integrates trapping data from yellow and blue sticky boards and sex pheromone lures with meteorological models. It will dynamically predict pest population density and optimize pesticide application windows.

Multi-source Integrated Pest Management (IPM): Screen for highly efficient natural enemy resources and establish a synergistic pest control model integrating "physical + chemical + biological" methods. Dynamically trigger differentiated, balanced pest control prescriptions to build an optimal closed-loop control model for pest and disease monitoring.

Screening of Precision Fertilizer and Pesticide Control Technologies: Establish a screening mechanism based on the criteria of environmental friendliness, economic feasibility, and operational convenience. Combined with the adjustment of water and fertilizer agronomic practices and pesticide management based on risk early-warning models, this will quantitatively evaluate the pesticide reduction effects and cowpea compliance rates.

5.Development of an Integrated Technical Scheme for "Monitoring - Early Warning - Control - Feedback"

Perception Layer: Utilizing a three-dimensional monitoring network composed of satellite remote sensing data analysis, UAV inspection data collection, and IoT sensors, the system will push real-time pest control recommendations via mobile apps or mini-programs.

Decision-Making Layer: Output dynamic pest control thresholds through a multi-factor coupled early-warning model integrating "cowpea growth stages, meteorology, and pests/diseases." Build an agronomic decision-making engine driven by an expert knowledge base to automatically generate parameterized solutions, such as pesticide mixing concentrations and UAV flight altitudes.

Interactive Feedback Layer: Through a mobile mini-program, provide three core functions: risk early-warning push notifications, an AI diagnostic assistant, and blockchain-based authentication for agricultural operation records.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Economic Cost Analysis

(1) Multi-dimensional Effectiveness Evaluation

Ecological Benefits: Monitor the reduction rate of chemical pesticides, the survival rate of natural enemy insects, and changes in soil organic matter content.

Quality and Safety: Compare the pesticide residue compliance rate, commercial fruit rate, and traceability information completeness between demonstration fields and conventional planting areas.

(2) Economic Cost Analysis of New Technologies in Cowpea Production and Quality Safety. Conduct a comparative analysis between cowpea planting plots within or near the demonstration bases that utilize the new technology and conventional plots that do not.

TOR for the Consulting Advisor's Work on Research of AI-Based Digital Standardized Aquaculture Technology Model (Contract No.: GDCS-020) under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

To facilitate the organization and implementation of the agricultural product quality and safety research under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project (hereinafter referred to as the "World Bank Loan Project"), and to ensure the successful completion of the project in accordance with its objectives and schedule, the Guangdong Center for Agricultural Product Quality and Safety (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) intends to hire a consulting advisor to conduct research on the AI-based digital standardized aquaculture technology model.

I.Background

As a vital component of China's agricultural economy, the aquaculture industry is a key sector for ensuring food security and optimizing dietary structures. With the continuous upgrading of consumer demands for aquatic product quality and increasingly stringent ecological and environmental protection policies, the traditional extensive aquaculture model can no longer meet the requirements of high-quality development. Particularly in terms of quality and safety supervision, aquaculture still faces prominent challenges, such as opaque production processes, delayed risk early warnings, and difficulties in tracing key indicators.

Due to its unique industrial characteristics, aquaculture still exhibits significant shortcomings in digital supervision practices. On the one hand, the dynamic and ever-changing aquatic environment involves multi-dimensional spatial interactions across the upper atmosphere, surface water bodies, and underwater ecosystems, making it difficult for traditional single monitoring methods to achieve full-scenario coverage. On the other hand, aquatic activities are characterized by concealment and suddenness. Traditional monitoring methods suffer from limited scope, untimely information acquisition, difficulty in identifying hidden behaviors, insufficient data accuracy, and high labor costs. These issues make the establishment of a standardized aquaculture system an urgent priority.

The core of this research lies in utilizing modern information technologies to achieve intelligent management of agricultural product quality and safety. Traditional production monitoring methods still face issues such as incomplete information collection and delayed responses to risk early warnings. To better address these challenges and further promote the digitalization of agricultural product quality and safety supervision, there is an urgent need to rely on modern information technologies—including AI, big data, IoT sensors, and cloud computing—to continuously improve the regulatory system. This is particularly crucial for process supervision and quality traceability in aquaculture, aiming to achieve full-chain safety management from production to distribution. This will not only help enhance the market competitiveness of agricultural products but also lay a solid foundation for the sustainable development of agricultural product quality and safety.

 

II.Objectives and Tasks

(I) Objectives

To address the current issues in aquaculture, including restricted information collection, delayed acquisition of key indicators, and the difficulty of tracing growth processes that lead to insufficient quality and safety, this project proposes to carry out the Development of an AI-Based Standardized Aquaculture System. Building upon existing development advantages and targeting the modernization of aquaculture, the project will dynamically monitor the growth status of aquatic products and implement timely interventions. This will continuously enhance product quality and safety throughout the production process, ultimately establishing a standardized aquaculture system.

(II) Specific Tasks

This research utilizes integrated space-air-ground intelligent technology, combined with remote sensing meteorological inversion, to accurately forecast key meteorological factors for the next 7 to 15 days, providing data support for large-scale cowpea planting management. By leveraging deep visual technology and crop growth prediction models, the study forecasts cowpea growth trends and establishes a pest and disease risk early-warning system. This enables precise fertilizer and pesticide application, promoting green and precision pest control. Furthermore, demonstration sites will be set up to host technical observation and training sessions, ultimately driving the safe, green, and sustainable development of cowpea production.

1.SWOT Analysis 

Summarize the current application status and existing challenges of new technologies, including satellite remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, ground sensors, and AI, in aquaculture production. Taking into account the actual conditions of the aquaculture production areas in the project pilot city, and considering multiple factors such as policy, economy, society, and technology, identify specific areas for investigation and evaluation. Examples include cost-benefit analysis, user acceptance surveys, and technical reliability testing. Meanwhile, ensure that the analysis provides a solid basis for subsequent strategy formulation.

2.Development of Intelligent Recognition Algorithms for Aquaculture Status Based on Low-Altitude Sensing Technology

Utilize drones to capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with deep learning technology, accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics. The study will precisely extract the intrinsic correlations between image features and aquaculture status, effectively addressing the issues of untimely and imprecise perception in traditional monitoring methods. This will significantly enhance the timeliness and accuracy of aquaculture status monitoring, providing robust algorithmic support for the intelligent management of aquaculture.

3. Development of a Big Data-Driven Standardized Digital Aquaculture Management System

Integrate multi-source data to comprehensively analyze aquaculture growth processes, feeding records, and growth status early warnings, thereby achieving the digitalization of the aquaculture process. Meanwhile, based on time-series analysis and observation, monitor aquatic product quality in real-time and implement timely interventions to continuously provide quality and safety recommendations throughout the production process. Comprehensively map the complex relationships among the water environment, meteorological conditions, biological status, and aquaculture farming operations to establish a standardized digital aquaculture system. This will realize full-process digital and information-based management of aquaculture, thoroughly resolving industry pain points such as unsmooth information flow and untimely farming operations. Ultimately, it will ensure the quality and safety of aquatic products across the entire chain from source to terminal, driving the high-quality development of the aquaculture industry.

4.Exploration and Screening of New Technologies

Develop aquaculture status recognition algorithms that integrate remote sensing with low-altitude sensing. The remote sensing analysis will utilize drones to dynamically and automatically capture high-definition images or videos near automatic feeders. Combined with remote sensing technologies for aquaculture environment analysis, the system will accurately analyze aquatic product density, feeding behavior, health status, and pathological characteristics, thereby achieving refined aquaculture status recognition.

Screening Criteria: Focusing on core indicators such as technological maturity, cost-effectiveness, and environmental adaptability, the optimal technology portfolio will be determined through laboratory simulations and pilot validations.

5.Development of an Integrated "Space-Air-Ground-Water" Technical System

Hardware Layer: Deploy a satellite remote sensing monitoring network, UAV inspection systems, and IoT water quality sensors to achieve full-dimensional dynamic tracking and identification of aquatic product status and the environment in the production areas.

Platform Layer: Utilize an aquaculture big data cloud platform to integrate a multi-source data fusion engine, AI analysis modules (such as density recognition and disease prediction), and a visual decision-making dashboard, supporting synchronized access via both PC and mobile clients.

Application Layer: Implement an intelligent decision-making system. Based on inversion models and growth prediction algorithms, it will automatically generate agronomic recommendations such as feeding amounts and water replacement cycles, and push them to farmers via mobile apps or mini-programs.

6. Effectiveness Evaluation and Promotion & Application

Multi-dimensional Evaluation: Quantify evaluation indicators such as the water quality compliance rate and disease incidence rate. Select two typical aquaculture demonstration sites in the Pearl River Delta to conduct application demonstrations. Verify the technological effectiveness through comparative trials, thereby providing a complete technical solution for the Guangdong Aquatic Product Quality and Safety Enhancement initiative. This will strongly drive the digital transformation and high-quality development of the aquaculture industry, demonstrating robust competitiveness and development potential in the era of the digital economy.

Basic Requirements for Aquaculture Demonstration Bases: The pond aquaculture area must be no less than 200 mu. Bases must establish an agricultural product quality and safety management system in accordance with the law, produce in compliance with relevant agricultural product quality and safety standards, and maintain digitalized production records for agricultural products.

Intitulé : Recrutement d'un Consultant Individuel en appui au MEAH pour l'Élaboration du WASH Compact National de Madagascar.

  1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar, par le biais du Ministère de l’Eau, de l’Assainissement et l’Hygiène a reçu un crédit de l’Association Internationale de Développement (IDA), dans le cadre de mise en œuvre du Projet d’Amélioration de l’Accès à l’Eau Potable (PAAEP Madagascar), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce crédit pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Consultant Individuel en appui au MEAH pour l'Élaboration du WASH Compact National de Madagascar».
  2. L'objectif principal de la mission du Consultant Individuel est d'accompagner le MEAH dans la finalisation d'un Compact National WASH de Madagascar, document politique de haut niveau qui formalisera les engagements du gouvernement et de ses partenaires en matière d'eau, d'assainissement et d'hygiène à l'horizon 2030.

Conformément aux exigences minimales d'un WASH Compact dans le cadre de Water Forward, le document devra couvrir au minimum les trois dimensions suivantes :

  • Cibles d'accès réalistes : objectifs quantitatifs et géographiques d'accès à l'eau potable, à l'assainissement de base et à l'hygiène, à l'horizon 2030, déclinés par milieu (urbain/rural) et par groupes de population vulnérables.
  • Réformes de gouvernance et d’amélioration du secteur : actions, réformes, politiques, programmes ou textes législatifs à engager ou à finaliser d'ici 2030, en s'appuyant sur les acquis récents (PNEAH, OREA, Code de l'eau).

notice_text:
WEST AFRICAN POWER POOL

Project:  WAPP GHANA-CÔTE D’IVOIRE INTERCONNECTION REINFORCEMENT PROJECT

NOTICE OF INTERNATIONAL RECRUITMENT

Revised 23.8.2026

Consultant Services

Selection of individual consultant

Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

Financing: World Bank IDA

Don IDA No: E4040

Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV

Open to: All eligible individuals

Duty Station: Abomey-Calavi, Benin

Application Deadline: 24 September 2024

 

  1. CONTEXT

The West African Power Pool (WAPP) was created by the highest decision-making authority of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) at the Conference of Heads of State and Government of the Member States held in Lomé, in December 1999. The Headquarters of the WAPP Secretariat is in Abomey-Calavi, Republic of Benin.

The ECOWAS strategic objective being implemented by the West African Power Pool (WAPP) is based on a dynamic vision of integrating national power grids into a unified regional electricity market, so that such a mechanism would, over the medium and long term, ensure to the ECOWAS citizens access to adequate power quality at an affordable price, and enhance the economic development of the Member States including industrialization growth, Health and Education improvement, Poverty Reduction, various Employment Opportunities Creation, etc…

To achieve its vision of operationalizing a unified ECOWAS regional electricity market, the WAPP Information and Coordination Centre (WAPP ICC), a Department within the WAPP Secretariat has been designated to perform the functions of a System Market Operator (SMO) responsible for coordinating the reliability of the WAPP Interconnected Transmission System (WAPPITS) made up of the power systems of fourteen (14) ECOWAS Member Countries and administration of the regional electricity market.

To this end, the WAPP Secretariat with the support of the World Bank within the Project “WAPP Côte d’Ivoire Interconnection and operationalization of the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market” intends to reinforce staffing of the ICC Department by filling a key vacant position, that of a Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer

The Engineer will be selected competitively, and the successful candidates will be joining the current team in the Information and Coordination Centre (ICC) as it prepares to operationalize the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market.

2. ROLE OVERVIEW

Under the supervision of the Head of the System Operations Coordination Division, the Power System Data Management & Data Analytics Engineer is responsible for the management of the ICC's Power System Database. He/She extracts data from various sources (APIs, HIVE tables, and other structured and unstructured data sources) to process and store large volumes of data, ensuring their accuracy, consistency and security. He/She develops reporting dashboards and analytical tools to support the analysis of power system operations, and supports the design, testing and implementation of models and databases for all systems requiring the WAPP Network Model.

The detailed Job description for the assignment may be consulted and/or downloaded from the WAPP website at: www.ecowapp.org/en/tenders

The WAPP General Secretariat invites eligible Individual Consultants to express their interest in providing the required Services described in the Job decription. Interested Consultants must provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services by submitting: (a) a cover letter/motivation letter, and (b) an up-to-date detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV).

WAPP is an equal opportunity employer that offers equal chances to men and women. Qualified women are strongly encouraged to apply.  

3. LANGUAGE

Good oral and written communication skills in English and French  

4. DURATION OF MISSION

The successful candidate shall be offered an initial Consultancy Contract of approximatively 17 months from the beginning of the assignment ( i.e.until April 30, 2028). Upon completion of the World Bank funding, the position shall be absorbed by WAPP.

The beginning of the assignment is planned for November 2026

5. SELECTION METHOD

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the method of "Selection of Individual Consultants" described in the World Bank "Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (edition September 2025).  

6. SUBMISSION OF APPLICATIONS

Applications must be submitted exclusively by email and should bear the subject line: “Application for ICC Engineer- Reference: BJ-WAPP-568960-CS-INDV”.

Paper applications will not be accepted.

Applications may be submitted in either French or English and should be sent to: procurement@ecowapp.org

 Particular emphasis should be placed on references for relevant similar assignments previously carried out, which should be clearly highlighted and described.

Deadline for submission of applications:  September 24, 2026, at noon, 12:00 pm, Benin local time (GMT+1).

spos@ecowapp.org

With copies to:

cpm@ecowapp.org

 hdhra@ecowapp.org

Only shortlisted candidates shall be contacted for the next stage of the recruitment process.

The Federated States of Micronesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Pacific Islands Regional Oceanscape Program - Second Phase for Economic Resilience (PROPER), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services are for the assessment of existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps and the design of a recommended coastal fisheries data management framework for future implementation. The assignment will cover the four FSM States of Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae and is expected to take approximately 12 months.

The FSM Department of Resources & Development (DRD), in collaboration with State Fisheries Departments, NORMA , now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

1. Objective and Scope of the Assignment

The objective of the consultancy is to assess existing coastal fisheries data systems and gaps, and to design a recommended data management framework for future implementation. The following areas are not within the scope of the assignment: 1) training, 2) conduct ecological field surveys, 3) build databases, 4) validate protocols, or and 5) produce management recommendations. These activities are intended to be undertaken under subsequent consultancies.

Stage

Main Activity

Expected Output / Focus

Existing literature, research reports, available databases, catch and effort, landings, market, ecological data, and metadata catalogue.

Fact-finding and prioritization with State fisheries departments, research institutions, and communities; information disaggregated by gender, age group, and fishing role where feasible.

3

4

Recommended SOPs for catch, effort, market, and biological data collection aligned with SPC, WCPFC, and FAO ASFIS references.

Recommended database architecture, hosting, backup, user permissions, ownership, interoperability, sustainability, and accessibility arrangements.

Ukraine with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association (hereinafter referred to as the World Bank) have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation).

LEARN was designed to address critical issues and provide the necessary support to the education sector in accordance with the Strategic Action Plan of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine until 2027, approved by the Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 07.03.2024 No. 276 (hereinafter referred to as the Strategic Plan).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is implemented through a US$235 million loan provided by Bank resources, supported by loan enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN No 9721-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT No 7626-UA). On July 1, 2025, the Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT No 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT No TF0C5794). On December 19, 2025, the Grant Agreement (Additional Financing for Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Project) between UKRAINE and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (GPE GRANT No TF0D0613, URTF GRANT No TF0D0612) was signed in the amount of US$31.1 million.

More detailed information about the LEARN program is provided at  https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

The latest additional grant agreement provides for expanded support for reforms in the education sector, in particular by:

• financing activities for the development of preschool education;

• providing grant support of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) aimed at strengthening the institutional capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine to implement educational reforms.

In accordance with the provisions of the agreements concluded, the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine is responsible for the overall implementation, coordination, monitoring and reporting on the Project activities, in particular those aimed at strengthening the institutional management capacity of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine. Such activities include the provision of technical assistance, the development and implementation of information systems, conducting training activities in the field of vocational (technical) education, as well as the implementation of initiatives in cross-sectoral areas, in particular inclusive education, European integration, education infrastructure management and strategic planning.

The Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) is implementing comprehensive reforms aimed at aligning the education system with labour market needs, supporting economic recovery, and advancing Ukraine’s European integration agenda.

A key component of this reform is the introduction of professionally oriented upper secondary education, which integrates general education with early professional orientation and creates structured pathways between general secondary education, vocational education, and professional pre-higher education.

The regulatory and methodological framework required for this transformation has already been established, including:

  • adoption of the Law of Ukraine “On professional (vocational) education” (August 2025);
  • development of secondary legislation and regulatory acts;
  • approval of competency-based professional education standards;
  • entry into force of the State Standard of Specialised Secondary Education (Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine dated July 25, 2024 No. 851);
  • Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine dated 08.06.2026 no. 898);
  • Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums (Order of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine No. 675 dated 05.06.2023

 

Initial experience in developing model programs has demonstrated strong demand, high institutional interest, and significant scalability potential. At the same time, the system currently lacks a sufficient number of professionally oriented model programs across priority economic sectors, as well as adapted academic content aligned with professional pathways.

Given that the regulatory framework has only recently been finalised, this Assignment represents the first opportunity to implement curriculum transformation at scale within a fully operational legal and methodological environment.

Under the GPE-financed institutional capacity activities, MoES intends to engage a qualified Consultant to develop a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education. The Assignment shall be implemented over a period of six (6) months from the Effective Date of the Contract. The Assignment will enable rapid, scalable transformation of curriculum content, directly impacting over 37,000 learners in priority economic sectors and creating a foundation for nationwide implementation of professionally oriented upper secondary education.

 

The Assignment is expected to be implemented in line with World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and applicable Ukrainian legislation.

 

II. OBJECTIVE

The objective of the Assignment is to support MoES in developing a comprehensive, scalable and standardised set of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

Specifically, the Assignment is to develop forty-one (41) model programs of mandatory educational components by educational domains for four (4) specializations of professionally oriented specialised secondary education, namely, Construction, Engineering and Technology, Information Technology, and Medical specialization (aligned with priority economic sectors) under the State standard of profile secondary education.

The model programs should be aligned with professional standards, labour market needs and sectoral requirements, as well as provide a unified national approach to curriculum development and adaptation.

The Consultant shall achieve the above objective in full compliance with applicable regulatory and legal framework of Ukraine, including relevant regulations of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine, and procurement and implementation requirements of the World Bank.

III. SCOPE OF SERVICES

3.1 Overall Approach

The Consultant shall provide comprehensive technical, methodological and organisational support to MoES for the development of professionally oriented model programs for upper secondary education.

The Assignment shall build upon the existing regulatory framework developed by MoES.

The implementation logic shall follow a structured sequence:

  1. Mobilisation of the expert pool.
  2. Development of specialised model programs.
  3. Quality assurance and validation.

All activities shall ensure consistency, scalability, and alignment across programs.

3.2 Components

Component 1. Expert Mobilisation and Coordination

The Consultant shall mobilise and manage a structured expert pool and ensure effective coordination throughout all stages of the Assignment.

The Consultant shall:

  • mobilise and manage a structured expert pool including:
    • VE and PPHE educators;
    • scientific and research-pedagogical staff (academics involved in relevant fields of study); 
    • sectoral experts from industry;
    • methodological specialists from NMCs;
  • ensure balanced representation across sectors;
  • establish coordination mechanisms and workflows;
  • assign clear roles and responsibilities;
  • develop Quality Assurance Plan;
  • ensure timely delivery of outputs.

It is recommended that each Model Program draft be developed by a compact drafting team comprising at least two (2) Subject Experts (Non-Key Experts) responsible for its development.

Each Sectoral Expert shall coordinate all drafts of Model Programs  within the assigned specialization and responsible for:

  • methodological supervision;
  • coordination of drafting teams;
  • ensuring consistency across all Model Programs within the specialization;
  • ensuring compliance with the State Standard of Specialized Secondary Education, the Typical Educational Program and methodological guidance approved by MoES;
  • internal quality control before submission for independent review.

Subject Experts may contribute to the development of more than one Model Program draft depending on their qualifications and the implementation methodology proposed by the Consultant.

All experts shall be engaged on a contractual basis, with clearly defined deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations.

Component 2. Development of Specialised Model Programs

The Consultant shall develop forty-one (41) specialised model programs across four (4) specializations defined according to priority economic sectors in accordance with State standard of specialised secondary education, Typical educational program of specialised secondary education in a professional orientation and Procedure for Conducting Expertise, Providing Grades to Educational Literature and Curriculums.The four priority sectors are:

    • Construction;
    • Engineering and technology;
    • Information technology;
    • Medical

Each program shall:

  • integrate general education subjects into applied, sector-specific contexts;
  • align with professional standards and occupational requirements;
  • reflect labour market needs;
  • follow State standard of specialised secondary education and Typical educational program of specialised secondary education;
  • be developed in accordance with the academic integrity values.

The development of every model program draft shall be based on the Typical educational programme for professionally oriented specialised secondary education approved under Order 898 and on the corresponding Typical curriculum plan for each of the four profiles listed above. The list of mandatory educational components for which MPs shall be developed for each profile, together with the corresponding number of teaching hours, hours of independent work, ECTS credits and their distribution between the profile-adaptation cycle (year 1) and the profile cycle (years 2-3), is set out in Annex 1 to this ToR.

 

Each MP shall comply with the structure and content requirements established in the Typical Educational Programme and shall consist, at minimum, of the following four parts:

  • Title page – name of the ministry/institution; type of programme (model programme / programme based on a model programme / programme not based on a model programme); type of mandatory educational component (subject, discipline, integrated/crosssectoral/special course, module, etc.); programme title; education level; profile of study; educational domain(s); assessment benchmarks (basic or advanced); author(s); year of development;
  • Introductory part – author's concept and the role and significance of the component; relevance for the selected profile; aim and objectives aligned with the assessment benchmarks of the State Standard and with the chosen profile; references to the relevant educational domain(s) and to professional standards, occupational qualification characteristics or professional prehigher education standards used as a basis; crossreferences to other MPs jointly covering the same mandatory learning outcomes, where applicable; workload in hours and ECTS credits; structural elements; recommended forms of organising the educational process;
  • Main part – titles and workload in hours of structural elements (content lines, sections, topics); expected learning outcomes linked to, and retaining the indexation of, the mandatory learning outcomes of the State Standard; proposed content reflecting professionally oriented, sectorspecific contexts relevant to the profile; recommended learning activities and active/interactive forms of organising learning; recommended methodological support bearing the "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" grif;
  • Concluding part – strategy and methodological recommendations for achieving the expected learning outcomes; description of assessment tools and instruments; reference to possible alternative assessment systems.

 

Each MP shall be submitted in the following format: paper size A4 (210×297 mm); font Times New Roman; main text – 14 pt; tables, footnotes and supplementary text – 10–12 pt; line spacing – 1.0; continuous page numbering starting from the second page.

The total workload of each MP, expressed in hours and ECTS credits, shall correspond exactly to the figures established for the relevant educational component for the respective profile, as set out in Annex 1. Any deviation shall be justified in writing by the Consultant and shall require prior written approval by MoES.

Although the educational domains of the components listed in Annexes 1 are common to all profiles, the content of each MP shall be professionally oriented to the specific profile for which it is developed, in accordance with Section 4 of the Typical Educational Programme. In particular, each MP shall:

  • integrate the competency potential and core knowledge of the relevant educational domain(s), as defined by the State Standard, with applied, occupation specific contexts relevant to the profile;
  • be consistent with the values, cross cutting skills and recommended forms of learning activity described in the Typical educational rogramme.

The development cycle shall be completed within 90 working days.

Considering the large number of tasks included under this component, it may be practical to divide it into two implementation stages.

In accordance with the Quality Assurance Plan and MoES regulations the Consultant shall ensure the quality of all specialised model programs developed under this Assignment through a two-tier quality assurance system: (i) the Consultant's own internal quality assurance process, and (ii) the official State expertise and grif procedure administered by MoES and  in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes (MoES Order No. 675 of 5 June 2023).

Tier 1 - Consultant's internal quality assurance

The Consultant shall:

  • conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle;
  • ensure consistency of outputs across all profiles through centralised coordination by the Quality Assurance Expert;
  • develop all the outputs following the academic integrity values

The Consultant may conduct iterative internal review at each stage of the development cycle and/or organise independent blind peer review as part of the Consultant’s internal quality assurance processes.

Tier 2 - Submission for the official MoES grif procedure

Each MP shall be submitted by the Consultant, through MoES to Ukrainian Institute of Education Development for expertise and the grant of the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine," in accordance with the Procedure for Conducting Expertise and Granting Grifs to Educational Literature and Educational Programmes.

The Consultant shall note that, pursuant to paragraph 6 of Section IV of the Procedure, expertise of model programmes (as objects falling under subparagraph 3 of paragraph 5 of Section I of the Procedure) is exempt from the standard fee-based expertise mechanism. The Consultant's budget shall accordingly cover only its own internal quality assurance activity.

 Expertise process and timelines to be reflected in the Work Schedule

The Consultant's Work Schedule shall account for the following parameters of the official procedure:

  • expertise is conducted by at least two members of the relevant Commission and/or expert group, selected by a method of random selection with regard to their professional background, specialisation and place of work;
  • the Commission's reasoned expert opinion is to be expected within two months of submission, unless a different period is agreed;
  • where the Commission requires revision, the Consultant shall resubmit the revised MP together with a reasoned response to each comment within 30 calendar days of receipt of the extract from the Commission's protocol;
  • the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" is granted by MoES order and is valid for five years, expiring on 1 July of the relevant year;
  • upon granting of the grif, the MP is entered in the public Catalogue of Granted Grifs maintained by MoES and the Institution.

The Assignment shall be deemed complete in respect of Component 2 only once the full package of drafts of model programs has obtained the grif "Recommended by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine" and has been duly entered in the Catalogue, once each tranche of programs has obtained such confirmation. Evidence of the grant of the grif and of the Catalogue entry shall be annexed to the relevant Interim or Final Completion Report.

The draft of each report shall be submitted in electronic (Word/Excel and PDF) format to the Client’s email address specified in the Contract. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Georgia

Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor - Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (TCTC-GATE)

Loan No. 9981-GE

Project No. P513957

 

Assignment Title: SUPERVISION OF CONSTRUCTION WORKS FOR BADIAURI-CHALAUBANI (LOT 4) AND CHALAUBANI – BAKURTSIKE (LOT 5) ROAD SECTIONS OF TBILISI–BAKURTSIKHE–LAGODEKHI (KAKHETI) HIGHWAY

Reference No. (As per Procurement Plan): TCTC-GATE/CS/QCBS-01

Georgia has received financing from the World Bank (WB) towards the cost of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor - Georgia Accessibility and Transport Enhancement Project (TCTC-GATE) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, and related services and consulting services to be procured under this project. The Project is co-financed by Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). The financing agreement with AIIB is being processed and will be concluded in due course. 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the SUPERVISION OF CONSTRUCTION WORKS FOR BADIAURI-CHALAUBANI (LOT 4) AND CHALAUBANI – BAKURTSIKE (LOT 5) ROAD SECTIONS OF TBILISI–BAKURTSIKHE–LAGODEKHI (KAKHETI) HIGHWAY. The proposed road sections form part of the Tbilisi–Bakurtsikhe–Lagodekhi (Azerbaijan Border) international highway and constitute a major transit corridor connecting Tbilisi to the Kakheti region and onward to north-western Azerbaijan. The Badiauri–Chalaubani road section (Lot 4) is a four-lane divided motorway that starts at Chainage (Ch.) 52+540, immediately after the Badiauri Interchange of Lot 3, and ends at Ch. 75+100 beyond the planned Chalaubani Interchange. The total length of this section is approximately 21.7 km, with a design speed of 120 km/h. The Chalaubani–Bakurtsikhe road section (Lot 5) is a four-lane divided motorway that starts at Ch. 75+100 and ends at Ch. 84+217.05, with the driving lanes separated by a double-sided concrete barrier. This section begins after the new Chalaubani Interchange, has a total length of approximately 9.1 km, and is designed for a speed of 100 km/h.

The primary objectives of the consulting services (“the Services”) are as follows: (i) to review the detailed designs (ii)Function as the Engineer in administering the civil works contracts for Lot 4 and Lot 5 (hereinafter “the Contract”) and execution of all rights and responsibilities of the Engineer in accordance with the Conditions of the Contract (FIDIC Red Book Second edition 2017, reprinted 2022); (iii) Comprehensive supervision of project implementation activities carried out by the Contractors to ensure compliance with the drawings, technical specifications and various stipulations contained in the contract documents, with high standards of quality assurance in supervision and in the execution of works; (iv) Advice the Client on all matters concerning the contract management and support the Client to have the works completed within the stipulated time for completion and cost to the extent possible.

The consultant is estimated to provide 817 person-months (full-time field presence) of consulting services. The services will be provided over a period of 92 months (including 2 months for Design Review, 30 months of construction supervision and 60 months of Defects Notification Period including maintenance), commencing tentatively in Q2 2027.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.
